evidence.quote: **a capability negative is only as strong as the selector that produced its candidates, and from now on it has to name it.**

§27.6's capability test drew the **12 most structurally distinct** candidates from the generator pool and concluded a capability limit. Re-drawing them by the *measured* predictor instead — every screen-passing, source-driven sample from the P5-v7 and P5-v8 narrowband pools, 29 distinct graphs, 26 of them novel — **24 of 29 close the band match**, and one closes the whole gate.

rule: Name the selector that produced the candidates whenever recording a capability negative, and re-draw the pool by any newly measured predictor before believing it.

applicability.applies: Every 'the generator/search/loop cannot do X' claim, and symmetrically to positives (stage 27 held the rung-0 selector fixed across all four arms for exactly this reason).
applicability.not: One clean falsification instance. Note also the sibling failure this session recorded against itself: 'every design that closed both the band match and 22.3 dB of gain carried >=12 devices' was a true statement about which structures had been TRIED, not a property of the problem -- the swap mutant did it at 10.
